chapter: Childhood, family and the sounds of New Orleans
title: The wagon piano and the kid with the bucket
summary: A street piano on a wagon went from bar to bar, and a kid collected money from the bar patrons.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Then there was these guys with the piano. There was the organ grinder, but it was a piano, and he got in a thing... It was like a shaft, like a wagon, and he pulled it about to different bars of the time and played. You heard that. Generally, this guy had a kid with him, and this kid was taking a bucket. And when he'd play a couple of tunes,

he'd send the kid inside of the bar. Because the bar-flies and the neighborhood chicks who frequented the local bars, they would hear the latest tunes, and it was a novelty. And they would come by to listen, or come out the barroom and listen. Some monkey would come out and do a little step. You heard that and you stop that.
